arxiv-1611-04049.creator: Chuyang Ke, Yan Jin, Heather Evans, Bill Lober, Xiaoning Qian, Ji Liu, Shuai Huang
arxiv-1611-04049.description: Abstract Surgical Site Infection (SSI) is a national priority in healthcare research. Much research attention has been attracted to develop better SSI risk prediction models. However, most of the existing SSI risk prediction models are built on static risk factors such as comorbidities and operative factors.

arxiv-2109-13695.title: Motion Deblurring with Real Events
arxiv-2109-13695.creator: Fang Xu, Lei Yu, Bishan Wang, Wen Yang, Gui-Song Xia, Xu Jia, Zhendong Qiao, Jianzhuang Liu
arxiv-2109-13695.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fang Xu, Lei Yu, Bishan Wang, Wen Yang, Gui-Song Xia, Xu Jia, Zhendong Qiao, Jianzhuang Liu. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end learning framework for event-based motion deblurring in a self-supervised manner, where real-world events are exploited to alleviate the performance degradation caused by data inconsistency. To achieve this end, optical flows are predicted from events, with which the blurry consistency and photometric consistency are exploited to enable self-supervision on the deblurring network with real-world data.

arxiv-2210-03497.title: When one Logic is Not Enough: Integrating First-order Annotations in OWL Ontologies
arxiv-2210-03497.creator: Simon Flügel, Martin Glauer, Fabian Neuhaus, Janna Hastings
arxiv-2210-03497.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Simon Flügel, Martin Glauer, Fabian Neuhaus, Janna Hastings. In ontology development, there is a gap between domain ontologies which mostly use the web ontology language, OWL, and foundational ontologies written in first-order logic, FOL. To bridge this gap, we present Gavel, a tool that supports the development of heterogeneous ’FOWL’ ontologies that extend OWL with FOL annotations, and is able to reason over the combined set of axioms.

arxiv-2402-05306.title: Interactive Symbolic Regression through Offline Reinforcement Learning: A Co-Design Framework
arxiv-2402-05306.creator: Yuan Tian, Wenqi Zhou, Michele Viscione, Hao Dong, David S. Kammer, Olga Fink
arxiv-2402-05306.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuan Tian, Wenqi Zhou, Michele Viscione, Hao Dong, David S. Kammer, Olga Fink. Symbolic Regression (SR) holds great potential for uncovering underlying mathematical and physical relationships from observed data. However, the vast combinatorial space of possible expressions poses significant challenges for both online search methods and pre-trained transformer models. Additionally, current state-of-the-art approaches typically do not consider the integration of domain experts’ prior knowledge and do not support iterative interactions with the model during the equation discovery process.

arxiv-2503-11116.creator: Hanbyul Song, Miguel F. Santos Silva, Jaume Suau, Luis Espinosa-Anke
arxiv-2503-11116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hanbyul Song, Miguel F. Santos Silva, Jaume Suau, Luis Espinosa-Anke. Understanding why people trust or distrust one another, institutions, or information is a complex task that has led scholars from various fields of study to employ diverse epistemological and methodological approaches Isaeva et al. Despite the challenges, it is generally agreed that the antecedents of trust (and distrust) encompass a multitude of emotional and cognitive factors, including a general disposition to trust and an assessment of trustworthiness factors Baer et al.

arxiv-2503-16382.title: Sparse Nonparametric Contextual Bandits
arxiv-2503-16382.creator: Hamish Flynn, Julia Olkhovskaya, Paul Rognon-Vael
arxiv-2503-16382.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hamish Flynn, Julia Olkhovskaya, Paul Rognon-Vael. We study the benefits of sparsity in nonparametric contextual bandit problems, in which the set of candidate features is countably or uncountably infinite. Our contribution is two-fold. First, using a novel reduction to sequences of multi-armed bandit problems, we provide lower bounds on the minimax regret, which show that polynomial dependence on the number of actions is generally unavoidable in this setting.

arxiv-2506-19467.title: Can Large Language Models Capture Human Annotator Disagreements?

arxiv-2506-19467.description: Abstract Human annotation variation (i.e., annotation disagreements) is common in NLP and often reflects important information such as task subjectivity and sample ambiguity. While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for automatic annotation to reduce human effort, their evaluation often focuses on predicting the majority-voted ‘‘ground truth’’ labels.

pmc-10689045.creator: Shanika L Amarasinghe, Phil Yang, Oliver Voogd, Haoyu Yang, Mei R M Du, Shian Su, Daniel V Brown, Jafar S Jabbari, Rory Bowden, Matthew E Ritchie
pmc-10689045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). scPipe is a flexible R/Bioconductor package originally developed to analyse platform-independent single-cell RNA-Seq data. To expand its preprocessing capability to accommodate new single-cell technologies, we further developed scPipe to handle single-cell ATAC-Seq and multi-modal (RNA-Seq and ATAC-Seq) data. pmc-10739346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023).
